payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image render its visual content as a pencil drawing overall?
node.criteria: Pass if the image as a whole is recognizably rendered in a pencil-drawing style, with pencil-like marks shaping the depicted content; some retained photographic detail or residual color does not by itself prevent a pass. Fail if it remains predominantly photographic or otherwise does not read overall as a pencil drawing, even if it is desaturated or has isolated sketch-like texture. Unknown if the edited image is unavailable or the overall style cannot be determined.
node.binding: Judge the overall rendering against the requested pencil-drawing outcome while checking that the visual content remains represented. Do not require complete removal of photographic detail or color, and do not treat isolated texture alone as sufficient.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image retains the depicted meal and table setting, while the overall scene has muted, grainy pencil-like shading and drawn contours. It reads as a pencil drawing despite some residual color and photographic detail.

fulfillment: The node’s completion rule is too permissive: it treats s1’s broad “overall pencil drawing” pass as sufficient for yes, even though the trace notes residual color and photographic detail and the reference is partial. Refine the binding/criteria so completion requires evidence that the requested transformation is substantially realized across the image, while retaining the depicted content; use s2 to assess remaining requested progress when s1 does not establish completion. Do not infer partial merely from residual color or from the reference label: inspect the image evidence and distinguish genuine incomplete transformation from acceptable pencil-style variation. The skipped s2 is a conditional dependency, not a transport failure; its invalid/unqueried status is not negative visual evidence. Preserve unknown when evidence is insufficient, and avoid making confidence alone determine the outcome.

response.content: {"text":"The trace supports real, broad pencil-style progress: the meal and setting remain recognizable, with grainy shading and drawn contours. Tighten the completion criterion to assess whether pencil marks and tonal rendering consistently replace the original photographic/color rendering across the scene, while allowing incidental color or detail that does not undermine the transformation. Keep partial distinct from both no progress and complete fulfillment; do not infer partial solely from the reference label or residual color. Route to the conditional remaining-progress check when this node establishes progress but cannot establish completion, and preserve unknown if visual evidence is insufficient. The skipped check is not negative evidence or a transport failure; confidence alone should not decide the label."}
